decision.observation: 5 mph in gear R, timer 45:14.646, dots pale. Camera swung to a high overhead view: the car sits on grass right of the gravel, nose angled up-frame roughly parallel to the road, with the white house with barn doors on the right and the road curving up-frame to a junction.
decision.hypothesis: The nose is already aligned along the road's run, so a plain-W conversion should carry the car forward along the grass and let it drift left onto the gravel without steering during the conversion bleed; steering now would push it right into the house's trees.
decision.memory: Post-fence recovery completed in two reverse beats totalling ~2.2 s without overshoot. High overhead views flip the steer sign less often than low diagonals, but keep re-deriving from the nose vs. road relation each frame.
